title: Basic statistics on a list of numbers
description: Write a function `stats_summary(numbers)` that returns a dict with keys `mean`, `median`, `mode`, `range` (max - min), `variance`, and `std` (population variance and standard deviation), using the `statistics` module.

hints: Module to consider: statistics, specifically mean(), median(), mode(), pvariance(), pstdev()
Each of these is a one-function answer to one question - statistics.mean(numbers), statistics.median(numbers), and so on, rather than a formula written out by hand for each.
Build the dict from statistics.mean, statistics.median, statistics.mode, max(numbers) - min(numbers), statistics.pvariance, and statistics.pstdev, one call per key.
expected_behavior: Returns a dict with mean, median, mode, range, variance, and std.
explanation: The statistics module already implements each of these measures correctly (including edge cases like even-length medians) - reimplementing mean/median/mode/variance by hand would just be re-deriving what the standard library already provides.
